summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly where data lives, eliminating costly data movement for training, inference, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Capabilities range from in-database SQL-based model training (BigQuery ML, Redshift ML, Aurora ML) to native vector search and managed LLM access (Snowflake Cortex, Databricks Mosaic AI, MongoDB Atlas). Gartner projects that by 2026, 30% of enterprises will rely on vector-based retrieval for GenAI, and the vector database market is forecast to reach ~$17.9B by 2034 at a ~24% CAGR.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI — managed LLM functions, Cortex Search, and Cortex Analyst
databases.description: Cortex provides serverless SQL and Python functions for LLM tasks (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), access to hosted foundation models (Llama, Mistral, Claude, Snowflake Arctic), plus Cortex Search for hybrid semantic retrieval and Cortex Analyst for natural-language-to-SQL. Snowflake also offers managed Postgres with Cortex AI integration to run AI directly alongside transactional data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a built-in VECTOR data type with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY / VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE functions and the fully managed Cortex Search service for semantic/hybrid search — no external extension required.
databases.llm_integration: First-party hosted LLMs via Cortex functions (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic, and others) callable directly from SQL/Python; Cortex Agents orchestrate structured and unstructured retrieval.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based: Cortex LLM functions billed per token/credit, vector and search operations consume Snowflake credits. No separate license; costs scale with usage and warehouse/serverless compute.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI and Gemini integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, matrix factorization, boosted trees, deep models) using standard SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI for generative models (Gemini), remote model inference via ML.GENERATE_TEXT / ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, and AutoML, keeping compute next to the data warehouse.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports a VECTOR_SEARCH function with vector indexes (IVF/TreeAH) and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING for generating embeddings in-place — a built-in capability.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI and Gemini models through remote models; ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING call hosted LLMs directly from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Billed via BigQuery compute (on-demand per TB scanned or capacity slots) plus Vertex AI charges for generative/remote model calls. Vector index storage and embedding generation incur standard BigQuery costs.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector for vector similarity and pgai for in-database LLM/embedding workflows
databases.description: Open-source PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds a vector data type with HNSW and IVFFlat indexes for similarity search, while pgai (from Timescale) brings embedding creation, RAG, and LLM calls (OpenAI, Ollama, etc.) directly into SQL. This 'keep everything together' approach lets developers run semantic search alongside relational data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native-via-extension on core Postgres. pgvector is the de facto standard extension providing true vector search with ANN indexes; it is not part of the base engine but is first-class and widely supported across managed Postgres offerings.
databases.llm_integration: Via pgai and related extensions, Postgres can call external LLM and embedding APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Ollama, local models) from SQL functions to power RAG and generation.
databases.pricing_notes: Extensions are free/open-source; cost is the underlying Postgres compute/storage (self-hosted or managed) plus any external LLM API usage fees.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning — SQL-based integration with Amazon SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications using familiar SQL by calling Amazon SageMaker endpoints, Amazon Bedrock foundation models, and Amazon Comprehend (for sentiment/NLP) directly from queries. It passes rows to the model and returns inferences without exporting data, ideal for real-time scoring on transactional data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively built into Aurora ML itself. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition is available only through the third-party pgvector extension, which is separate from the Aurora ML inference service. Aurora ML provides model inference, not native vector indexing.
databases.llm_integration: Through Amazon Bedrock integration, Aurora ML can invoke foundation models (e.g., for text generation/embeddings) and SageMaker-hosted models via SQL functions like aws_bedrock.invoke_model.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional Aurora ML charge for the SQL integration; you pay for underlying Aurora capacity plus the called service (SageMaker endpoints, Bedrock tokens, or Comprehend requests).

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML — in-warehouse model training and inference via SageMaker and Bedrock
databases.description: Redshift ML enables data analysts and scientists to create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL CREATE MODEL statements, powered by Amazon SageMaker Autopilot and Neo under the hood. It supports regression, classification, and bring-your-own-model remote inference, and can invoke Amazon Bedrock LLMs for generative tasks on warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Redshift ML focuses on predictive model training/inference; Redshift does not provide a built-in production vector search/ANN index equivalent to dedicated vector databases. Embedding generation is possible via Bedrock integration, but native vector indexing is not a core feature.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI and embeddings, and with SageMaker-hosted LLMs, all invokable from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: No separate Redshift ML license; you pay Redshift compute/storage plus SageMaker training/hosting costs (for in-Redshift local models, inference runs within the cluster) and Bedrock usage when used.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) with Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides an end-to-end platform for building, fine-tuning, serving, and governing ML and generative AI models, including Foundation Model APIs, AI Functions in SQL, agent frameworks, and MLflow lifecycle management. Databricks Vector Search provides a managed, serverless vector index synced with Delta tables for RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in, fully managed vector database that automatically syncs embeddings from Delta tables and supports hybrid (keyword + semantic) search.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs host open models (Llama, DBRX, Mixtral) and provide external-model gateways to OpenAI/Anthropic; LLMs are callable via SQL ai_query functions and agent frameworks.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) for compute, model serving, and Vector Search endpoints; Foundation Model APIs billed per token (pay-per-token or provisioned throughput).

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search for semantic retrieval and RAG
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search lets developers store embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and run approximate nearest-neighbor queries using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage with HNSW indexing. It supports pre-filtering, hybrid search, and integrates with popular AI frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) for building RAG applications on operational data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Vector search is a built-in Atlas feature using dedicated vector search indexes and the $vectorSearch operator — no external vector database required.
databases.llm_integration: No hosted LLMs of its own; integrates with external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Hugging Face, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI) and orchestration frameworks to generate embeddings and power RAG.
databases.pricing_notes: Available on Atlas dedicated clusters; vector search runs on Search Nodes or cluster resources, billed as part of Atlas consumption (cluster tier/compute and storage). No separate per-query license.
